filters.digestFull: {omitted} do not fit (at most {limit} memories or 9,000 characters) and are not read at session start. Untick what every session does not need.

login.title: Unlock Mimers Brain
login.description: Paste the access key. It is exchanged for a cookie that remains in this browser, so you only do this once.

editor.description: Write it as a standalone statement that any AI can understand much later without the original context.
editor.title: Title
editor.pinnedHint: Every connected model reads the digest first, once per session. Preferences and profile memories are included unless unticked. Only confirmed memories are shown. Pin only what a model would get wrong without it, across many different tasks; search finds everything else.

thought.pinnedHint: In the session digest every model reads first
thought.pinnedWaitingHint: Pinned, but only confirmed memories go into the session digest. Confirm it on the Review page.
thought.copyRefHint: Copies the memory's id and title. Paste it into a chat with any model and say what to change.
thought.restoreConfirm: Put back the fields as they were before this change?

ingest.title: Review proposed memories
ingest.description: Nothing has been saved yet. Edit or deselect proposals before applying them.

pending.title: Trust review
pending.description: Agent-generated memories remain evidence until you confirm how they may be used.

rarelyUseful.title: Rarely useful
rarelyUseful.description: Returned by search again and again, but never used in an answer. Possibly outdated, too vague or wrongly worded. Confirm keeps the memory as it is and resets its count.

duplicates.title: Possible duplicates
duplicates.description: Semantically similar memories are suggested here but never changed automatically.

recalls.title: Recall receipts
recalls.description: Shows only client and memory ids — never the query or answer.

contradictions.title: Possible contradictions
contradictions.description: Two current memories about the same item that a language model thinks cannot both be true. New pairs are checked every night; nothing is changed automatically.

deleted.title: Recently deleted
deleted.description: A deleted memory can be restored for {days} days. After that only the record of the delete remains.
deleted.forgetConfirm: Remove every kept copy of this text now? The memory can then no longer be restored.

tiers.vaultOption: 🔒 Vault — sensitive context and SECRET_REF pointers

brain.title: The brain
brain.description: Every current memory and what connects it to others. Memories that mean similar things sit in the same region. The more connections, the larger the memory and the deeper inside it sits.

health.title: Memory health
health.description: What can be trusted and used now, separated from historical and archived records.

recall.title: Recall quality
recall.description: Privacy-safe receipts show whether clients report their searches and whether returned memories helped.

activity.title: Activity
activity.description: Calls, clients and created records. No query, answer or memory content is logged.

operations.title: Operations
operations.description: Publishing and integration health for the service around the memory.

kpi.noneOverdue: no receipt older than ten minutes

chart.reportedResultsPerDay: Use of reported results per day

clients.title: Which clients read and write
clients.description: MCP reports the client application, never the model answering inside it — that information simply is not on the wire. If a client has no name in its handshake, its user agent is used instead.
clients.empty: No traffic has been logged yet.

recall.clientsDescription: Only client identity, counts and UUID receipt completion are recorded — never the query or answer.
recall.since: Recall statistics start on {date}, when privacy-safe receipts were introduced. Earlier calls are deliberately not treated as missing receipts.
recall.noData: Recall statistics begin with the first privacy-safe receipt. Earlier calls are deliberately not treated as missing receipts.

mqtt.title: MQTT to Home Assistant
mqtt.notConfigured: Not configured. Set MQTT_URL (and, when needed, MQTT_USERNAME / MQTT_PASSWORD) in .env on the server and restart it. The brain will then publish its vital signs and counters. See the README for the entities created in Home Assistant.
mqtt.publishFailed: Could not publish — the broker is not connected.

retention.label: Keep usage events and recall receipts for
retention.confirm: {count} usage events and recall receipts are older than this and will be deleted permanently. Statistics for that period disappear with them. Continue?
retention.note: Only affects the usage log and the recall receipts. Memories are never pruned.

stats.footer: Timezone for day and month boundaries: {timezone}. Usage events and recall receipts are retained for {days} days and never contain queries, answers or memory content — only aggregate activity and UUID receipt state.

brain.hint: Drag to turn · scroll to zoom · grab a memory to see its connections

connect.fetchError: Could not load the connection details.

policy.title: One policy for every model
policy.description: MCP clients get a short version as server instructions when they connect, and the full policy from memory_digest at the start of each session. Paste the full text into the client's global or system instructions if it does not support MCP server instructions.
policy.note: Keep this text unchanged so every client follows the same retrieval, capture, supersession and secret-handling rules.

addresses.title: The three addresses
addresses.description: The vault is served only by the first address and stores sensitive context and SECRET_REF pointers. Raw passwords, tokens and keys must never be stored in either tier.
addresses.unknownLan: not known yet — open this page once on the LAN and the server will learn its address
addresses.lanWhen: on the LAN or over VPN
addresses.publicWhen: everywhere else, and for every other model
addresses.readWhen: for a model that may look things up but must not change them
addresses.viewing: You are currently viewing the {listener} (Mimers Brain {version}).

keyCard.title: Keys
keyCard.openUrlOnly: open tier only, and only as ?key=
keyCard.readOnlyOpens: open tier, read only – no tool that writes exists on that port
keyCard.readNotSet: not set – the read-only port falls back to MCP_ACCESS_KEY
keyCard.remoteWarning: The vault key is shown only on the LAN address. Sending it through the proxy would put the one credential that unlocks the vault in the browser cache whenever the page opens. Retrieve it on the server:

claudeCode.title: Claude Code
claudeCode.description: Register both addresses as separate entries. The memory then works even when the laptop is away from the LAN — open tier only, but better than nothing. The change takes effect in the next session.

codex.title: VS Code (Codex)
codex.description: The editor opens the connection from your own machine, so the LAN address works and gives access to the full vault. The model answering does not affect access, but it does affect content: every vault row returned by a tool enters the context and is sent to the model provider on the next turn. Use the public address instead if that is not appropriate.
codex.environment: Keep the key out of the config file
codex.note: Set MIMERS_VALV_KEY as a user environment variable and restart the editor so the extension inherits it. The codex binary lives inside the extension and is not normally on PATH.
codex.policyNote: As a fallback, put the copied policy in ~/.codex/AGENTS.md. Codex reads global AGENTS.md guidance at the start of each run.

claudeDesktop.title: Claude Desktop — chat connector
claudeDesktop.description: The dialog accepts only a URL and has no header field. The key therefore travels in the URL, which is why it must be a different key: URL credentials are saved in client configuration and proxy logs. This key reaches only the open tier and can be rotated independently.
claudeDesktop.oauthNote: If an authenticator is in front, /.well-known/oauth-* must answer 404, not redirect to a login page. Otherwise the client assumes an OAuth server exists and fails before the URL key is used.

openWebui.title: Open WebUI
openWebui.description: Mimers Brain has a native OpenAPI tool surface beside MCP, so Open WebUI needs no translation proxy.
openWebui.note: Use MCP_ACCESS_KEY as the token. The URL points directly to Mimers Brain; no mcpo translation proxy is needed.

readOnly.title: Read-only connection
readOnly.description: Port 8792 serves the open tier with no write tools registered at all. A model on it can search, list, fetch and read statistics, and has no way to save, replace, review or delete a memory. Use it for models that do not look after the memory well.
readOnly.urlKey: Address with the key in the URL, for clients with no header field
readOnly.openapi: OpenAPI document, for Open WebUI and similar
readOnly.note: Give this key out on its own. A client that also holds MCP_OPEN_KEY or MCP_ACCESS_KEY can simply write on another port.
readOnly.proxyNote: To reach it from outside, forward a second hostname to port 8792 in Nginx Proxy Manager, exactly as you did for 8791.

otherClients.title: ChatGPT, Gemini and others
otherClients.description: The same principle applies everywhere: an MCP server over HTTP with a bearer token. The search and fetch tools exist for clients that expect the simpler search-and-fetch shape. Never use the LAN address here — it is not remotely reachable, and making it so would expose the vault to a third party.

remoteVault.title: Need the vault in an HTTPS-only client?
remoteVault.description: Do not open the port. mcp-remote runs as a local stdio server, reaches the LAN address over ordinary HTTP and adds the header itself.

verify.title: Verify the connection
verify.note: {count} tools in the response means everything works. 401 means the key is wrong. A 302 to the authenticator means the proxy is incorrectly sending /mcp through forward auth.

toolDescriptions.search_thoughts: Search by meaning. The important one.
toolDescriptions.list_thoughts: Recent memories filtered by type, topic, person and time
toolDescriptions.preview_ingest: Preview atomic memories from a longer source
toolDescriptions.report_memory_usage: Report which recalled memories were used
toolDescriptions.supersede_thought: Replace memories while preserving navigable history
toolDescriptions.search: Search in the shape ChatGPT and Gemini expect

models.title: Models
models.description: Which provider and model each job uses. Only shown on the LAN listener, because these models read vault memories too.

roleHint.embedding: Search, the recall hook and every save
roleHint.metadata: Title, summary and facets on save

models.embeddingWarning: A new embedding model embeds every memory again in the background. Search keeps the current model until you switch, and nothing changes if you cancel.
models.reembedConfirm: Embed every memory again with {model}? Search is not affected until you switch.
models.thresholds: The similarity thresholds - search 0.3, recall hook 0.5, duplicates 0.86, contradictions 0.6 - were measured with text-embedding-3-small. Another embedding model may score higher or lower; compare a few searches before switching.

migration.title: Re-embedding with {model}

status.ready: Ready. Compare, then switch or cancel.

migration.failed: {n} could not be embedded and will be retried after the switch
migration.compareHint: Ask the same question of both models. The scores are not comparable between models; look at the order.
migration.comparePlaceholder: A question you know the answer to
migration.switchConfirm: Switch search to {model}? The old vectors are removed.
migration.cancelConfirm: Cancel and remove the new vectors?

providers.title: Providers
providers.unreadable: stored key cannot be opened - enter it again
providers.name: Name
providers.keySaved: Saved - type a new one to replace it
providers.keyFromEnv: From .env - type one to use another here
providers.keyNote: Stored encrypted with SETTINGS_KEY and never shown again. Keep a copy in your own secret store; an empty field keeps the current key.
providers.noSettingsKey: Set SETTINGS_KEY in .env once to store keys from this page. Addresses work without it.
providers.clearConfirm: Remove the address, name and key set here? Whatever .env says applies again.
